proofs.full_local_argument: Since ||y||<=R/2 and h<=R/2, ||y+h e_i||<=||y||+h<=R, and y is also feasible. For each i, differentiability gives f(y+h e_i)-f(y)-h partial_i f(y)=integral_0^h <grad f(y+t e_i)-grad f(y),e_i> dt. Cauchy–Schwarz and gradient Lipschitzness bound its absolute value by integral_0^h beta t dt=beta h^2/2. Dividing by h>0 gives |[g_h(y)]_i-partial_i f(y)|<=beta h/2. Thus ||g_h(y)-grad f(y)||^2=sum_i |[g_h(y)]_i-partial_i f(y)|^2<=d beta^2 h^2/4; taking square roots gives the claim. For delta>0 the chosen h is positive, <=R/2 and <=2delta/(beta sqrt(d)), hence error <=delta. There are d displaced values and one shared base value. With no stored values this is d+1 oracle calls. If f(y) is already stored exactly, it is reused without a call, so at most d additional calls suffice. These steps use neither convexity nor minimizer assumptions. Exact arithmetic is essential to the stated error budget, which has no observational or rounding error term.

assumptions: f:R^d->R is C^1 with globally beta-Lipschitz gradient in Euclidean norm.
The oracle returns exact f values; y in C and 0<h<=R/2.
Convexity, existence/uniqueness/location of a minimizer are not needed for this local calculation.
statement.conclusion: y and all y+h e_i belong to X, and ||g_h(y)-grad f(y)||_2<=beta h sqrt(d)/2. The displayed choice gives norm error <=delta. Computing the estimate needs d+1 exact values if none is cached; a stored exact f(y) reduces new calls to d (and other exact-point caches may reduce calls further).
statement.objects_and_definitions: X=B_2^d(R), C=B_2^d(R/2), e_i the standard Euclidean basis. For y in C and h>0 define [g_h(y)]_i=[f(y+h e_i)-f(y)]/h. This local smooth-only formulation generalizes the source Lemma 4.1, which states it for f in F_beta(d,R).
statement.parameter_domains: d in N; R,beta>0; ||y||<=R/2; 0<h<=R/2. For target norm error delta>0 choose h=min{R/2,2delta/(beta sqrt(d))}.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every d>=1,R,beta>0, every such f,y,h, the deterministic vector estimate satisfies the conclusion. No probability or function-gap assertion.
